SIMP

Symplectic Integrators for Monte-carlo Proposals.

SIMP integrates Hamiltonian systems and builds the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo proposals that run on them. Symplectic integrators conserve a nearby energy, so a trajectory holds its total energy over long horizons and the proposals it produces are accepted at high rates.

The integrators are splitting schemes: an alternating sequence of position and momentum updates whose coefficients define the method. Leapfrog and the Yoshida order 4, 6, and 8 members come from a single triple-jump composition, so the whole family shares one stepper and one coefficient source. Adding a scheme is one registry entry. A two-stage member, minerror2, uses the kick weight (3 - sqrt(5)) / 4 that cancels the leading energy error on a Gaussian target, which makes it the accurate choice for Hamiltonian Monte Carlo on near-Gaussian posteriors.

For non-separable Hamiltonians, such as Riemannian dynamics with a position-dependent mass, simp_integrate_nonsep() uses the generalized (implicit) leapfrog.

The steppers are a header-only, scalar-templated C++ core. Consumers link against it with LinkingTo: SIMP and drive it with a native gradient under automatic differentiation, so the same code path serves plain-double integration and gradient-based inference engines.

Install 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("gcol33/SIMP")

Integrate a trajectory 

library(SIMP)

# Unit Gaussian target: U(q) = 0.5 q'q, so grad_U(q) = q.
grad_U <- function(q) q

out <- simp_integrate(
  q0 = c(1, 0), p0 = c(0, 1),
  grad_U = grad_U, eps = 0.1, n_steps = 60,
  integrator = "yoshida4"
)
out$q

simp_schemes() lists the built-in integrators with their order and gradient cost per step.

Sample with HMC 

Sigma <- matrix(c(1, 0.8, 0.8, 1), 2)
P <- solve(Sigma)
U <- function(q) 0.5 * as.numeric(t(q) %*% P %*% q)
grad_U <- function(q) as.numeric(P %*% q)

fit <- simp_hmc(U, grad_U, init = c(0, 0), n_iter = 2000, eps = 0.2,
                n_steps = 20, warmup = 500, integrator = "leapfrog")

colMeans(fit$draws)
fit$accept_rate

Pass any name from simp_schemes() as integrator to compare schemes on the same target.
